meta.title: Episodic memory without autonoetic consciousness
meta.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 379:20230410
meta.domain: Philosophy of mind / philosophy of memory — autonoetic consciousness and episodic memory
meta.overview: A theoretical/philosophical argument that autonoetic consciousness is neither a valid construct nor necessary for episodic memory. Marshalls clinical dissociations (aphantasia, SDAM, cases J.V./M.L./R.B.) and factor-analytic evidence to argue phenomenology is a contingent feature of retrieval, and proposes a 'topology of memory' model plus a return to a functional/computational characterization of episodic memory.
meta.abstract: This opinion piece argues that the construct of autonoetic consciousness lacks validity and is not necessary for episodic memory. Drawing on factor-analytic results (Remember/Know responses do not load with re-experiencing), clinical dissociations (aphantasia, SDAM, and cases who recollect without a sense of ownership), and developmental/comparative considerations, it proposes that the phenomenology typically associated with episodic memory is a contingent property of the retrieval process, determined by the 'topology' of a memory, and advocates returning to a functional/computational characterization of episodic memory.

claims.statement: The construct of autonoetic consciousness lacks validity.
Autonoetic consciousness is not necessary for episodic memory (patients recollect specific events without a sense of ownership/re-experiencing).
The phenomenology associated with episodic memory is a contingent, not necessary, property — determined by the 'topology' of the memory.
Episodic memory should return to a functional/computational characterization, enabling developmental, comparative (non-human) and artificial-agent work.

entities.term: Topology of a memory (threshold of subjectivity)

contributions.typing_rationale: Introduces intentional-objects-vs-contents and conceptual-vs-non-conceptual-contents distinctions to explain when memory phenomenology arises.
Proposes a topology-of-memory model in which conscious 'flavour' depends on content strength crossing a threshold of subjectivity.
Synthesizes Tulving's 40-year trajectory and clinical dissociations into an argument for a functional/computational account of episodic memory.

sota.resolver_notes: Undermind semantic search (year_max=2024) surfaced Carruthers 2018 ('Episodic memory isn't essentially autonoetic') as the closest finding-level prior (nearly the same thesis) and Klein 2013 (recollection as a retrieval operation). Zaman et al. 2024 supplies contemporaneous empirical support (R/K as strength); Tulving 1985 is the position refuted. Moderate-to-high overlap on the bare thesis — the novelty is the topology-of-memory model and functional reframing, not the claim that autonoesis is dispensable.
